# R3 Pass-One Visual / Taste Review Reviewer identity: Claude Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`), fresh rationale-quarantined visual/taste reviewer; no author rationale, no prior critic output, no R2 or lifecycle files consulted. Exact source commit: bdeb338372bf4ef29cb8d683e07ea840acdb4681 Exact artifact SHA-256: 5edb72222f7d6e96c43a5f577ee735487047c9067762c2f0033130c6262c7062 Verdict: BLOCK Packet integrity: recomputed `shasum -a 256 artifact/reference-r3.html` = `5edb7222…c7062`, matching `ARTIFACT_SHA256` and the `artifact_sha256` in `evidence/browser-proof.json`. All 53 files in `FILE_INDEX.txt` are present. ## Artifact-changing blockers **1. Severity: High — Japan's sparkline asserts a large gain directly above its own loss figures and "Reduce risk now" (default shipped state).** Evidence: `artifact/reference-r3.html`, Act 2 card `data-performance-market="JP"`; rendered in `evidence/proposal-r3-organ-stale-dark-en.png`, `evidence/proposal-r3-organ-stale-light-en.png`, `evidence/proposal-r3-desktop-dark-en.png`, and every default desktop/mobile capture. The Japan polyline (viewBox `0 0 200 40`) starts at y=40.0 — its own series minimum — and ends at y=17.0, a **+58% of chart height upward** move, stroked *and* area-filled with `var(--up)`. The same card simultaneously reports `data-usd="-4.8"`, `data-local="-7.2"`, a `state-danger` chip reading "Breaking down", and the stance "Reduce risk now". The element's own `aria-label` is "Recent change shape" and the panel caption states "Change shape uses the committed recent price path." No horizon reading rescues it: Japan is negative in both USD and local terms at 3M. The other six cards are directionally consistent, and all seven paths are unique (not copy-paste filler), so this is a mis-bound series, not decoration. User-visible failure: in the single most important comparison organ, a reader scanning shape-first sees Japan as the recovering market while the numbers and the engine say it is the one to cut. Direction color is inverted against fact in a page whose whole premise is engine-owned honesty. Minimum repair: rebind Japan's polyline to the committed Japanese price path for the selected horizon and derive `stroke`/`fill` from the sign of the displayed return rather than a hardcoded `var(--up)`. **2. Severity: High — the "change shape" sparkline is frozen and never tracks the horizon selector, producing further sign contradictions on an evidenced interaction.** Evidence: the `[data-horizon]` click handler in `artifact/reference-r3.html` rewrites only `[data-value="usd"|"local"|"fx"]` and calls `syncHorizonLabels`; it never touches the sparkline. Confirmed at pixel level: diffing `evidence/proposal-r3-desktop-dark-en.png` against `evidence/proposal-r3-desktop-dark-en-horizon-12m.png` changes only 78 of 6736 rows, and every band carrying sparkline stroke pixels (y 1111–1140, 1324–1336, 1345–1351) is **byte-identical** between 3M and 12M. User-visible failure: selecting 1M leaves JP, EZ, GB and AU — four of seven cards — showing rising, gain-colored shapes against negative USD returns (−1.0, −4.6, −3.1, −4.8); 6M leaves GB and AU contradictory. The horizon control is a headline interaction with its own committed captures, so this is on the demonstrated path, not a corner case. Minimum repair: carry a per-horizon path in `data-returns` and redraw on horizon change; if per-horizon paths are unavailable, drop the color/fill encoding and relabel the graphic to a fixed, explicitly-stated window so it stops asserting the selected horizon's direction. **3. Severity: Medium — untranslated English strings render inside the Chinese locale, in Act 1 beneath the verdict.** Evidence: `artifact/reference-r3.html` — `
Dragged by 🇯🇵 Japan · 🇮🇳 India · 🇪🇺 Eurozone
`, `
🇺🇸 USWorld 🌍
`, and the metric value `Jul 2023` all lack any `.l-zh` sibling, so they cannot render in Chinese. Visually confirmed: rasterising y 663–679 of `evidence/proposal-r3-desktop-light-zh.png` renders the glyph run "Dragged by … Japan · India · Eurozone" in Latin type surrounded by Chinese copy. User-visible failure: the Chinese reader meets raw English in the highest-value block on the page, and the same three economies are correctly localised elsewhere (日本 / 印度 / 欧元区), so the page contradicts its own translation standard. Contract item 4 names "no bilingual token leakage" explicitly. Minimum repair: wrap the three strings in `.l-en`/`.l-zh` pairs reusing the existing country and date translations. ## Material findings **A. The eight international-stocks preservation captures cannot support a non-regression claim.** In all eight, the page's own content is rendered at markedly reduced ink amplitude while the persistent chrome is crisp. Measured strongest content ink vs. strongest chrome ink: desktop dark 103 vs 255, desktop light 157 vs 61, mobile dark 163 vs 209 — content/chrome amplitude ratios of 0.35–0.85. Controls taken with the same metric show no such gap: every R3 capture reaches 243 (dark) / 35 (light), and the production baselines reach 209 / 61. The stocks H1 "International Stock Dashboard" sits at roughly 2.4:1 against its background. This is the signature of a capture taken before the content settled. Separately, `baseline/` contains only the eight `intl.html` captures described in `baseline/baseline.yml`; there is **no production-before stocks capture**, so "without visual regression" has no comparand — even though `baseline.yml` itself flags that `intl_stocks.html` shares `templates/intl.html.j2` behind `mode == stocks`, which is precisely the shared-template risk this evidence exists to retire. Re-capture after settle, plus a stocks baseline, before adjudicating item 10. **B. Latent locale defect in the horizon labels (not visible in the supplied captures).** All seven `[data-horizon-label]` spans are hardcoded `3M`, and `syncHorizonLabels` is invoked only from the horizon and language click handlers — never at initialisation. The captures are clean: rasterising the market-index line confirms "3月" in `proposal-r3-desktop-light-zh.png` and "3M" in the English twin, so the harness reached Chinese via the 中文 button. But a page served with `data-lang="zh"` already set — the normal production integration path — would render seven English "3M" labels until the reader clicks something. Repair: give the spans `.l-en`/`.l-zh` pairs, or call `syncHorizonLabels` once on load. **C. Two same-colored circular scores compete for the first answer.** The preserved upstream band shows `61` with "Risk-on, narrowing" at 24px in `--status-good-ink`; Act 1 shows the engine-owned `66` with "Risk-on" at 22px in the same token. The R3 numeral is larger (34px vs 24px) and the H1 separates the two, so the hierarchy holds — but the upstream *headline* is two pixels larger than the R3 verdict word and identically colored, and "Risk-on, narrowing" versus "Risk-on" is a distinction a scanning reader will not draw. The disambiguation currently rests entirely on 10px eyebrow text. Worth a deliberate divergence in weight or hue for the upstream band. **D. The organ-state captures cannot evidence their own locality assertions.** `browser-proof.json` asserts `unrelated_rotation_visible: true` and `unrelated_deep_desks_visible: true` for all eight degraded-state captures, but those files are cropped to the organ (1404×299–750) and show nothing else. The claim does hold structurally — state switching is scoped to `.organ[data-state=…]` and only `data-organ="global-pulse"` carries states — but the images are not the proof the JSON implies. ## Requirement audit 1. **Six-act hierarchy and legible first answer around 66/100 — PASS.** Acts 1–6 present and numbered in source; `actCount: 6` in all 25 R3 captures. The gauge arc is geometrically honest: `dasharray 257.6` / `dashoffset 87.6` = 0.6599 filled, i.e. exactly 66/100. The 66 numeral (34px) outweighs the upstream 61 (24px). Qualified by material finding C. 2. **Institutional density without sprawl or score theater — PASS.** Panel weights genuinely vary (gauge card, 7-up pulse grid, dense 13-column macro table, 2-up deep desks); no equal-weight museum. One gauge, drawn to true value; sparklines are 42px; no decorative hero charts. Seen across `proposal-r3-desktop-dark-en.png` and the light/zh twins. 3. **Independently authored dark and light art directions, readable light ink — PASS.** Light is not an inversion: it introduces its own darker ink ramp (`--ink-up #116c3a`, `--ink-down #a72424`, `--ink-warn #754800`, `--status-good-ink #17653e`) and its own shadow recipe, against dark's lighter ramp. Measured contrast on `--panel`/`--panel2`: body text 16.27/14.44, muted 5.27/4.68, all status inks 6.28–8.94; light chips on their own mixed backgrounds 6.17–7.48. 4. **True EN/ZH typography and no token leakage — FAIL.** Typography is otherwise disciplined — PingFang SC stack, `letter-spacing:0` reset for CJK eyebrows/chips/headers, zero CJK found inside any `.l-en` span, and the only Latin inside `.l-zh` spans is legitimate proper nouns (IMF, WEO, PCE, GDP, Prophet, Berg–Pattillo). Blocker 3 is the failure. 5. **Semantic color behavior — PASS.** `html[data-lang="zh"]` redefines only `--up`, `--down`, `--ink-up`, `--ink-down`; `--status-danger/caution/good/neutral` are never touched in any locale rule, and grep confirms `--up`/`--down` are used *only* in sparkline strokes/fills and `--ink-up`/`--ink-down` *only* in `.dir-up`/`.dir-down`. Verified empirically: a status-ink palette census across `country-gb-light-en/zh`, `gb-dark-en/zh` and `jp-light-en/zh` shows identical status-ink pixel populations with no swap, while direction colors do correctly flip (sparklines green in EN → red in ZH). This separation is cleanly done. 6. **Desktop 1440 / mobile 390 recomposition — PASS.** `scrollWidth == clientWidth` in all 41 captures (1440/1440, 390/390): no accidental horizontal scroll. Mobile edge scan finds no clipped content — the only ink reaching x=0/389 is the fixture banner's own full-bleed border (y 71–154), symmetric left/right. Three breakpoints collapse grids to 1–2 columns; the two wide tables (`min-width` 720px / 1180px) sit in deliberate `overflow-x:auto` wrappers and both fit uncropped at desktop's 1372px content width. 7. **Honest null, stale, loading, empty, error, local to the organ — PASS.** All four degraded states verified in both themes. Stale keeps every value visible with an explicit disclosure; loading uses skeletons and states "the remaining five acts stay available"; empty and error both name what failed and what still works. Typed nulls are excellent: Taiwan renders `—` for curve/real-10Y/CPI/GDP/unemployment while showing a literal `0` for recession pressure, honoring "Missing is a state, not zero." See finding D for the evidence-scope caveat. 8. **Country inspector across seven countries with visible selected/focus state — PASS.** Seven tabs and seven panels with correct `role="tab"`/`tabpanel`, `aria-controls`, `aria-selected`, roving `tabindex`, and wrap-around arrow-key handling matching every `keyboard_next` in the proof. Captures exist for all seven. Per-country detail reconciles exactly to the cross-country row (spot-verified JP, EZ, TW, GB across themes and locales). Selected state = link-tinted background plus link-colored border; focus = 2px outline at 3px offset — both clearly visible in `proposal-r3-country-jp-dark-en.png`, `-ez-dark-en.png`, `-tw-dark-en.png`, `-gb-light-zh.png`. 9. **Horizon selection clarity and locale labels — PASS (on the captured evidence).** Five horizons with `aria-pressed`, active state clearly distinguished. Glyph-level rasterisation of the market-index line confirms "3月" in the Chinese capture and "3M" in the English one. Qualified by material finding B. Note that blocker 2 concerns what the horizon control *fails to update*, not the labels. 10. **Separate international-stocks preservation without regression — NOT PROVEN.** See material finding A: the captures show unsettled content in both themes, both locales and both viewports, and the packet carries no stocks baseline to compare against. ## Non-blocking notes - The error state and the empty state share identical neutral chrome (`--panel2`, dashed `--line`); nothing but the sentence distinguishes a failure from a legitimately empty result. A severity cue on error would cost nothing and the tokens already exist. - The fixture harness controls (`REFERENCE STATE` · Default/Loading/Empty/Stale/Error) and the preserved shell's theme buttons (Dark/Light) stay English in the Chinese locale. Both are reference/preserved-shell scope rather than R3 product surface, so I did not count them as leakage — but the fixture controls do sit inside the Act 2 panel and are visible in the Chinese captures. - At mobile the fixture banner is full-bleed to x=0/389 while all other content carries a 10px gutter, so its 10px corner radius is clipped by the viewport edge. Cosmetic, fixture-only. - `--muted` at 4.68:1 on `--panel2` in light is the thinnest ink in the system and is used at 10–11px for eyebrows, table headers and captions. It clears AA, with no margin. - The Act 1 caveat lists Eurozone among the three draggers, but at the default 3M horizon EZ (+1.2%) ranks above AU (+0.3%) and roughly ties GB (+1.3%). This may be correct against the gauge's own 200-day-line receipt rather than 3M USD return; it is not resolvable inside this packet, so I raise it only as something a data reviewer should confirm. - The fragility map renders six of seven rows as the identical string "No concurrent structural warning". Honest, and arguably the point, but it reads as dead weight at full-page scale; a collapsed "6 of 7 clear" summary with the one exception promoted would carry the same information with less pagespace. ## Review integrity I used only the contents of `/private/tmp/intl-r3-review-visual-bdeb338`. I read `REVIEW_BRIEF.md` first, then `artifact/reference-r3.html` directly (full CSS, body markup and script), `baseline/baseline.yml`, `evidence/browser-proof.json`, and the baseline and evidence images. Image analysis was performed in-memory with PIL/numpy on packet files only; no crops, derivatives, or scratch files were written anywhere, and no path outside the packet was read or created. I received no author rationale and no prior review, and I did not read or seek `proposal.yml`, `verdict.yml`, `approval.yml`, R2 materials, or any repository outside this packet. I treated `browser-proof.json` as evidence to audit rather than as a verdict — and two of my findings (A and D) are challenges to its sufficiency. I modified no file; this review is my only output.
